text:
Nazem Kadri is back where he won a Stanley Cup in 2022, and at 36 he's still getting to the places that matter. Sportsnet and The Denver Post both wrote last week about his new line with Gabriel Landeskog and Nicolas Roy finding its feet in Toronto, of all places, where his career began.

He has 5 goals and 18 points in 23 games on 18 minutes a night, 8 of them on the power play. The goals are the part that lags: 5 on 9.4 expected, and none in his last seven games on 3.9 expected. That's a finishing slump, not a player running out of chances. Goals tend to follow looks like that. Colorado gets about 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, a little better than without him.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking backs up what the chance numbers say: last season he was among the better forwards at getting to the slot, setting up teammates and exiting his own zone with the puck. We'd watch his minutes, down about two a night over the last ten games, while the goals catch up.
